summary: New two-independent-Radon-branch full-mass equations: FULL D finite iff sum integral tail^(3/2) finite; actual decreasing C/G presentations. Unbounded full-nonskeletal example E=-7/3,D=25/6. Whole Dirac coalescence fails only within this family.
detailedSummary: Each branch may independently have mass up to one. Actual same-branch fixed-fibre products and n1 cross vanishing give the finite constructions; tensor convex combinations, local uniform closure and decreasing cutoffs give arbitrary Radon depth measures. E=-1/3-(S1+S2)/3 and FULL D=1/6+2(S1+S2)/3, with a canonical actual presentation-generated operator. M1=M2=1 eliminates Gauss mass entirely. Moving distinct-residue family measures and weak limits have at most one unit in any fixed ordinary residue bidisc, so they cannot yield the whole2delta_x target. This is restricted progress, not general analytic recognition, arbitrary-support existence or all-G uniqueness.
text:
Using earlier OWN n1 for its reconstructed actual continuous calculus, there is a larger new full-nonskeletal-mass sector: TWO independent arbitrary Radon depth distributions. This is not repetition of the earlier one-branch result with off-Gauss mass at most one. Retain the two distinct-residue centres, actual ordinary charts, original entire C, cubic energy/full dual and actual presentation-generated G of n1.

Let zeta_i be finite positive Radon measures on (0,infinity), each with M_i<=1. Let T_i(t)=zeta_i((t,infinity)), d_i(c)=int_0^c sqrt(T_i(t))dt, S_i=int_0^infinity T_i(t)^(3/2)dt. Define the actual positive Radon target of raw mass two
mu=(2-M1-M2)delta_g+sum_i (c->x_i,c)_*zeta_i.
The Gauss branch maps are continuous by their polynomial maximum-norm formula (and the unit-coordinate Laurent extension). Compact depth restrictions are Radon pushforwards; total-variation approximation by these restrictions proves regularity of the full finite pushforward. No mass is placed at infinite-depth Pi.

THEOREM: FULL D(mu)<infinity iff S1+S2<infinity. If finite, q=q0-d1(gamma1)-d2(gamma2) has ACTUAL continuous decreasing C presentations q_n=q0-sum_i int_0^min(gamma_i,n) sqrt(T_i(t))dt, finite lower energy, and canonical presentation-generated MA(q)=mu. Its energy is -1/3-(S1+S2)/3, its prescribed moment is -1/2-S1-S2, and FULL D=1/6+2(S1+S2)/3. It is bounded continuous iff BOTH int sqrt(T_i) are finite; otherwise it is extended continuous with poles exactly at the centres whose integrals diverge. When M1=M2=1, all two units of measure are nonskeletal, including unbounded finite-energy cases.

Here is the needed same-branch current reconstruction, not taken as a grant from supplied notes. For c<d, the local translated maxima L_c,L_d have product supported at g and x_i,c. At polynomial zeros omit the zero slots; both locally use only the remaining coordinate, giving zero square. On the unit-coordinate locus, put b_j=log|w_j|. Where one b_j>=0, both maxima locally agree with the common three-plane maximum; its square is the previously identified inverse-coordinate Gauss atom. In the negative quadrant, if m=max(b1,b2)<-c, L_c is constant; if m>-c, both equal m and are rank one. At m=-c and b1!=b2, L_d is a single unit logarithm. At b1=b2=-c, DD L_d=DD log max(1,|w1/w2|) is the fixed ratio Gauss curve by CLD18.6.2, d=1. On it, over H(eta1), L_c restricts to log max(exp(-c),|w2|). The proper fixed-fibre restriction and the curve d=1 formula give a singleton. Its iterated Gauss norm is the original joint norm because (j,k)->(j,j+k) is a bijection of Laurent exponents, determinant one. Thus B(q_i,c,q_i,d)=delta_g+delta_x_i,min(c,d), on every analytic test. Equal depths are n1's square. Cross-branch Delta_1,c Delta_2,d=0 is n1's newly proved identity.

For finite depths c_i,1<...<c_i,N and masses m_i,k, set alpha_i,k=sqrt(sum_j>=k m_i,j), alpha_i,N+1=0, beta_i,k=alpha_i,k-alpha_i,k+1. On each branch, beta and 1-sqrt(M_i) form a probability over depth slots and zero correction. Tensoring the two probabilities represents q0+sum_i,k beta_i,k v_i,c_i,k as a positive convex combination of ACTUAL two-well corner weights from n1. Hence membership in the ENTIRE original C is proved. The same-branch product gives coefficient beta_i,k^2+2 beta_i,k sum_j>k beta_i,j=alpha_i,k^2-alpha_i,k+1^2=m_i,k, and n1's cross identity removes every interbranch contribution. The remaining Gauss coefficient is 2-M1-M2. The correction on a branch equals -d_i(gamma_i), by differentiation between depths and value zero at depth zero. Tonelli gives int d_i(c)zeta_i(dc)=int sqrt(T_i(t))zeta_i([t,infinity))dt=S_i, because atomic endpoints affect no Lebesgue integral. Actual first variation along the common scalar h gives E'=-h^2(S1+S2), proving the finite energy formula and target moment.

For each finite C, push every depth to min(c,C) keeping masses fixed. Approximate the resulting finite depth measures by partition masses placed at positive right endpoints. Their tails converge at all non-atomic thresholds, hence almost everywhere, and their square roots are bounded by one. Dominated convergence gives L1(0,C) convergence of the square-root tails. The finite weights converge UNIFORMLY, with error bounded by the sum of those L1 errors, to the actual q_C=q0-sum_i d_i,C(gamma_i). Original minimal-sheaf closure and recursive-product continuity prove q_C in C and its actual operator
MA(q_C)=(2-M1-M2)g+sum_i (c->x_i,min(c,C))_*zeta_i
against all continuous analytic tests. They also give E(q_C)=-1/3-sum_i S_i,C/3, where S_i,C=int_0^C T_i^(3/2). Tonelli gives its own target moment AND its moment against untruncated mu as -1/2-sum_i S_i,C.

The q_n are actual normalized, nonpositive, globally continuous and pointwise decreasing everywhere. Finite sum S_i supplies the finite lower energy antecedent for G. Their actual bounded MA measures converge weakly to mu with test error at most 2||h||infinity sum_i zeta_i((n,infinity)). The generated-operator fact below makes this canonical MA(q), rather than declaring positivity or MA for a Borel limit. Tonelli gives the finite prescribed moment. For each fixed a in ENTIRE C, n1's tangent inequality at q_n passes weakly to E(a)-int a mu<=1/6+2sum S_i/3. The bounded competitors q_n have objective exactly 1/6+2sum S_i,n/3, giving equality in FULL D. If sum S_i is infinite those same actual competitors force D=infinity; no operator is assigned to an ineligible limit. The continuity and pole assertions follow from the actual extended continuous gamma_i and their increasing integrals; near either centre the other correction is zero.

Generated canonicity retains ACTUAL antecedents. The span V of C is uniformly dense in C(X): write elements as A(p-q), fill convex averages with zero, and use max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A[max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-(q+s)/2] to see V is a vector lattice. It contains constants and separates actual points. Different tropical values are separated by small quadratic caps. At equal tropical values, a Laurent polynomial P with different seminorms gives different psi=log max(1,|P|/R) values. In an injective chart with centred rho0, the bounded collar cap w=max(0,delta+epsilon psi-rho0), with epsilon small and delta positive, is zero on the outer ordinary collar and separates the central points; rho0+w=max(rho0,delta+epsilon psi) proves actual positivity. Smooth convex ramps handle polynomial zeros. Separation plus constants matches any continuous h at a pair x,y; finite maxima over y and then finite minima over x on compact Hausdorff X approximate h uniformly. This proves density without a countable determining set.

For any actual b_n decreasing to v with finite lower energy, monotonicity gives a finite limiting energy. For another presentation c_m, fixed n and epsilon>0, the increasing open sets {c_m<b_n+epsilon} cover compact X. A finite cover gives one global m; monotonicity and E(b_n+epsilon)=E(b_n)+2epsilon prove energy independence in both directions. The same applies to finite convex combinations, whose lower bounds follow from concavity. For each bounded w, the cubics P_n(t)=E((1-t)b_n+tw) and A_n(t)=E(t b_n) converge at every t in [0,1]; four distinct parameters make coefficient limits canonical by interpolation. First variation gives int w MA(b_n)=P'_n(0)+A'_n(1), so its limit is canonical. The dense span, positive common mass two and uniform approximation extend this to all continuous tests. The compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation theorem gives the unique positive Radon measure of mass two, the canonical generated operator. This construction applies to the displayed q_n and does not manufacture a presentation for any unrelated measure.

Explicit new UNBOUNDED FULL MASS example: take zeta_i=c^-2 dc on [1,infinity) on EACH branch, each mass one. T_i is one below one and 1/t above, so S_i=3 but int sqrt(T_i)=infinity. The target int_1^infinity(delta_x1,c+delta_x2,c)c^-2dc has NO Gauss or other canonical-skeleton mass. The actual solution is q0-d(gamma1)-d(gamma2), with d(c)=c up to one and 2sqrt(c)-1 thereafter. It has poles only at P1,P2, E=-7/3, FULL D=25/6, and prescribed moment=-13/2. Its actual cutoff energies are -7/3+4/(3sqrt n).

Useful failed-coalescence conclusion: even allowing both centres and their eligible distributions to move, this constructed family and ALL its weak Radon limits have mass at most one in every FIXED ordinary residue bidisc D={|z1-a|<1,|z2-b|<1}. A positive-depth Gauss point belongs to D exactly when its centre has both residues (a,b); at most one of the two distinct-residue centres does, and that branch has mass<=1. Also g is outside D. For any continuous 0<=h<=1 compactly supported in D, weak convergence preserves int h<=1. Radon regularity and compact-Hausdorff cutoffs yield lambda(D)<=1. Thus no weak limit in this family equals 2delta_x_a,b,c for c>0, whose mass in D is two. This is only a constraint on this newly constructed family, not on ENTIRE C/G, and not a new general nonexistence result.

All proofs are in standalone.tex and proof-companion.txt; exact primary applications are in source-application-reading-ledger.json/.txt. Rerun: python3 checks.py > check-output.json; python3 package.py > package-output.json. The general dominated analytic recognition problem, arbitrary-support equations, single whole Dirac, new full-G uniqueness audit, and original P16.7 remain unresolved. Actual energy/operator presentations in this special sector are not a general compactness/envelope theorem. Independent correctness and compilation remain unverified.
